Diversity

/duh-VUR-si-tee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Diversity is state of having variety.

The city's diversity is reflected in its many different restaurants and festivals.

Worked Example

Snorkeling over the reef, the students count parrotfish, eels, seahorses, and dozens of coral shapes in every color. In one small stretch of water, no two creatures they spot seem to be of the same kind.

The reef's richness comes from containing so many different kinds of life at once, and that state of built-in variety is diversity. Diversity is more precise than 'difference' because it describes the overall condition of a group made up of many varied members, not just one contrast between two things.

How Diversity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

variety

variety: an assortment of different things

multiplicity

multiplicity: a large number of varied elements

heterogeneity

heterogeneity: the state of mixing different kinds

Antonyms

sameness

sameness: lack of variety; being all alike

homogeneity

homogeneity: the state of being one kind

How Strong Is It? — variation → variety → diversity → multiplicity

variation vs. diversity

variation vs. diversity: Variation is weaker than diversity — variation means small differences within one kind, while diversity means a whole range of truly different kinds.

variety vs. diversity

variety vs. diversity: Variety is weaker than diversity; a variety offers several options, but diversity suggests a rich mix of many distinct kinds, backgrounds, or forms.

multiplicity vs. diversity

multiplicity vs. diversity: Multiplicity is stronger than diversity — diversity means real differences within a group, while multiplicity emphasizes an almost overwhelming number of different elements.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of diversity.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — di-

prefix — di-: apart, in different directions (Latin (dis-))

root — vers

root — vers: to turn (Latin (vertere))

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state or quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Di- (apart) + vers (turn) + -ity (quality of): diversity is the quality of having 'turned apart' in different directions — many different kinds existing within one group.

Use the root in a new word: versatile

Use the root in a new word: versatile: A versatile athlete, she starred in three different sports.

Root Check

Word Choice

Diversity almost always describes a group or population, not an individual (racial diversity, diversity of opinion), and shows up often alongside verbs like 'promote,' 'value,' or 'lack' in conversations about inclusion.
